items.title: Fred Moore Interview, 1959-06-19
items.q: Eddie Dawson told me about this.

ctx.x: Shoe Shine's Rag. Yeah. Shoe Postal. Yeah. The 12s. Yeah. Then he'd hit one or two chords, demonstrate, tell them that's where you're going. That's when the band was going to sound when he starts. He'd hit a chord and explain to the people what that chord meant, what he was going to do, you know. When he start off, he start the band off, he never beat no, uh... Never beat the temple off modern like, uh, like the fellas do here in New York. He never beat no four beats. He stomped his foot down on, on the naked…

They still do that, down in New Orleans, I've seen this. Did you ever hear about Joe Oliver? One time he wanted the band to go out. That's happening to all this. Eddie Dawson told me about this. And they never would pay any attention. He'd stomp his foot, and that meant to go out, you know? Finish his foot. So, one day he had a brick in his trumpet case. So instead of stomping his foot, Frank threw it down on the floor. One beat means, one beat means that, after you finish the number, one beat means that you're…
Joe Oliver used to, well, he didn't do it. Well, he meant it, he meant business, but he called it rehearsal.
